$comment: The OpenSSL interoperability corpus (scripts/lib/pki-corpus.ts), declared: scripts/validate-pki.ts holds the table to these counts (a coverage canary), tests/tools/pki-corpus.test.ts holds this file to the table. OpenSSL 3.x is the external judge; every artefact is written by the BUILT server (dist/server.js) under a pinned instant.

levels.name: engine round trip
checks: inspect_certificate (self-signature or issuer signature) + verify_certificate_chain to the corpus CA at the pinned instant, with serverName and purposes for the leaves
inspect_csr with the proof of possession verified
verify_cms with the trust anchors (and the detached content)
decode_asn1 of the OCSP and time-stamp requests, plus an independent node:crypto reckoning of the CertID hashes / serial and of the message imprint / nonce
a deterministic entry produced twice hashes the same
a negative canary is refused with its declared code (a canary that writes bytes is an XPASS and fails the run)

levels.name: OpenSSL
levels.where: openssl 3.x on PATH (OPENSSL_BIN overrides; LibreSSL and OpenSSL < 3.0 are refused); skipped with the reason when absent, a failure under PKINATIVE_INTEROP_REQUIRED=1 or the gate's --require-all
checks: x509 -text dumps every certificate (DER) and every PEM re-encoding
verify reaches OK from each leaf to its corpus CA (-purpose sslserver for the leaves, -untrusted for the pathLen-0 intermediate), at -attime 2027-01-01
req -verify reports the self-signature OK for every request (DER and the PEM re-encoding)
crl -text dumps the PEM re-encoding of the intermediate CRL
cms -verify reports CMS Verification successful for the attached and detached signatures (-CAfile the fixture root; the Ed25519 signer against its own root)
ocsp -req_text prints the Serial Number of the OCSP requests
ts -query -text prints the Nonce of the time-stamp requests
